note: Written by Claude from reputable outlets (Reuters via syndication partners, AFP via The Star, Al Jazeera, ABC News, The Korea Herald, Yonhap via The Korea Times, SCMP, Xinhua, TechCrunch and others); source under each story. Saturday news flow was light, so several sections are shorter rather than padded. Disclosure: Claude is made by Anthropic, which appears in today's news. Sports excluded.

items.headline: Big Tech buybacks collapse as AI spending eats cash
items.summary: A Reuters analysis finds Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Oracle cut share buybacks 83% to $13.6bn in the first nine months of 2026, as capital spending doubled to $556.9bn and exceeded operating cash flow for the first time since at least 2011. Combined free cash flow swung to a $14bn deficit.

items.headline: OpenAI reportedly trims its funding target
items.summary: OpenAI has cut the target for its new funding round to $20bn from $30bn, the Financial Times reported, with UAE-based investors expected to lead. The Wall Street Journal said about $11bn has been secured so far amid a lukewarm response; the report also flagged possible headwinds for Anthropic's planned IPO.

items.headline: October ends with a thud for chip and AI stocks
items.summary: Friday's sell-off was the Nasdaq's biggest since June, with Sandisk down 13% after Intel's collapse and the hyperscalers off 1–2%. The Nasdaq 100 fell 3.5% and was nearing correction territory; Capital Economics says the four hyperscalers made up over a third of S&P 500 capex in the past year.

items.headline: Silver and gold extend their slide
items.summary: Silver fell 6% on Friday and is now down 31% for 2026, while gold lost 3.5% and is down 10% on the year. Oil rose 2% and Treasuries rallied as investors retreated from risk.

items.headline: Bank stocks and bitcoin caught in the risk-off wave
items.summary: Goldman Sachs fell 4% and Jefferies 6% in Friday's sell-off, while bitcoin slipped 3% after hackers took more than $6bn from Binance.

items.headline: China's factory gauge sinks to 49.3
items.summary: China's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October from 50.1, missing a 50.0 forecast and marking a third contraction in four months; the services-and-construction index also dipped to 49.7. Economists blamed weak home demand and fading front-loaded export orders.

items.headline: Rupee posts its best month in eight
items.summary: India's rupee closed Friday at 94.95 per dollar, up about 1% for October, helped by central bank steps to curb dollar demand, including supplying dollars directly to state oil firms. High oil prices and portfolio outflows remain headwinds.

items.headline: PAL cancels some Singapore–Manila flights around Asean summit
items.summary: Philippine Airlines is cancelling or rescheduling several flights to and from Manila, including Singapore services, between Nov 14 and 18 as delegates arrive for the 49th Asean Summit. Affected passengers can rebook free, take a full refund or convert to a travel fund.
items.source: Philippine Daily Inquirer/ANN via The Star

items.headline: Melaka campaign opens in test for Anwar
items.summary: Campaigning began in Malaysia's Melaka state after all 79 nominations were accepted for the 28-seat assembly, with polling on Nov 14. The vote tests Anwar Ibrahim's coalition, which lost recent state polls in Johor and Negeri Sembilan, as UMNO and PAS deepen cooperation.

items.headline: China helps break up regional meth network
items.summary: China says it worked with Indonesia and Malaysia to dismantle a major transnational methamphetamine trafficking network in Southeast Asia.

items.headline: Manila declares special days for Asean summit
items.summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr declared Nov 16–18 special non-working days in Metro Manila as the Philippines hosts the 49th Asean Summit and related meetings.
items.source: Philippine Daily Inquirer/ANN via The Star

items.headline: Myanmar sets 34 public holidays for 2027
items.summary: Myanmar's state gazette lists 34 public holidays next year, including a nine-day Thingyan New Year break from April 10 to 18.

items.headline: Tokyo, Seoul and Washington vow 'complete' North Korean denuclearisation
items.summary: Foreign ministers Toshimitsu Motegi, Cho Hyun and Marco Rubio reaffirmed the goal at talks on the sidelines of a G20 meeting in Atlanta, and pledged to enforce UN sanctions. The pledge comes amid speculation about a Trump–Kim meeting at next month's APEC summit in China.

items.headline: Lee doubles down on review of multicultural family benefits
items.summary: President Lee Jae Myung said support for multicultural families should continue but that policies causing 'reverse discrimination' should be fixed, citing priority access to state postpartum care centres and daycare admission points. Liberal critics warn the debate could stoke hatred.
items.source: The Korea Herald / Yonhap via The Korea Times

items.headline: Over 7,800 police deployed for Halloween crowds
items.summary: Police deployed more than 7,800 officers to 28 heavily managed zones nationwide, including Itaewon and Hongdae, for Halloween weekend crowds.

items.headline: Seoul's freeze proposal shadows denuclearisation pledge
items.summary: Alongside the trilateral vow, AFP notes Lee proposed in September that Washington seek a freeze of North Korea's nuclear programme in exchange for sanctions relief, which critics say risks tacitly accepting a nuclear North.

items.headline: Markets see 80%+ chance of RBA hike on Tuesday
items.summary: Markets put the odds of a Reserve Bank rate rise on Melbourne Cup Day above 80%, which would take the cash rate to 4.85%, the highest since 2008. Pressure is building on Labor over spending ahead of December's mid-year budget update.

items.headline: Albanese heads to Commonwealth summit in Antigua
items.summary: The prime minister is travelling to CHOGM in Antigua and Barbuda, where leaders will discuss climate, AI regulation, trade and slavery reparations; he will meet UK PM Andy Burnham and Canada's Mark Carney. The Coalition criticised the trip as households face a likely rate rise.

items.headline: Residents rally against 1,200MW AI data centre in SA
items.summary: Locals near Tungkillo, east of Adelaide, protested Quantum DC's proposed 1,200-megawatt AI data centre over water, land-use and noise concerns, backed by the Liberals, Greens and One Nation. No development application has been lodged yet.

items.headline: Early vote tops 43 million before midterms
items.summary: An AP analysis counted more than 43 million early in-person and mail ballots five days before Tuesday's election, nearly 10 million more than at the same point in 2022. Texas and Georgia are running well ahead of their 2022 pace.

items.headline: Democrats hold 8-point generic ballot lead
items.summary: RealClearPolling's average shows Democrats ahead 51.4% to 43.2% on the congressional ballot; analysts see the House as likely to flip but the Senate as far less certain. An Emerson poll has a Democrat narrowly leading in Kansas's Senate race.

items.headline: US joins allies in denuclearisation pledge
items.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio and his Japanese and South Korean counterparts reaffirmed the goal of North Korea's complete denuclearisation, as Trump signals openness to meeting Kim Jong Un.

items.headline: Factory activity contracts as demand cools
items.summary: October's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3, with production and new orders below 50; small and medium firms contracted while high-tech manufacturing held at 51.3. Officials blamed demand pulled forward before the National Day holiday.

items.headline: Reverse repo becomes main policy rate from Monday
items.summary: From Nov 2 the overnight reverse repo rate becomes China's main policy rate, and planners are drafting a 2026–2030 strategy to expand domestic demand.

items.headline: Trade surplus on track to beat last year's $1.2tn
items.summary: Reuters notes China's trade surplus is heading past last year's record, while Q3 growth of 4.5% keeps the annual target within reach without fresh stimulus, though economists are urging more support.

items.headline: Modi declares Naxalism defeated on Unity Day
items.summary: Speaking at Ekta Nagar on Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, Modi said his pledge to end Maoist insurgency had been met, warned of 'Dimagi Naxals' spreading unrest online, and accused the opposition of obstruction. He also said India had shielded citizens from the worst of the global energy crisis.

items.headline: RBI's dollar curbs lift the rupee
items.summary: The rupee gained about 1% in October, its best month since February, after the RBI redirected oil companies' dollar buying away from the spot market and tightened hedging rules.

items.headline: Cotton import duty waiver extended to year-end
items.summary: The government extended the customs duty exemption on cotton imports, due to lapse on Oct 31, until Dec 31 to ease input costs for textile makers.
